newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UNHCR urges Kabila to protect Rwandan refugees.
newsitem.headline: UNHCR urges Kabila to protect Rwandan refugees.

text.p: The U.N. refugee agency on Tuesday urged Congo President Laurent Kabila and the Organisation of African Unity to take measures to protect Rwandan refugees after a Save the Children worker and four refugees were killed near Goma.

Spokeswoman Pam O'Toole said the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) was suspending its aid work at Karuba, in the east of the Democratic Republic of Congo (formerly Zaire), where armed men were reported to have killed the five on May 29, although their bodies have not yet been found.

Karuba is an important "collection point" for Rwandan refugees west of Goma, who gather on their way home after hiding out in the forest. About 25,000 people transitted through Karuba in March and April, although O'Toole said the numbers had dropped to a "trickle".
"The Save the Children Fund worker, a child he was carrying and three adult refugees were reported killed," the UNHCR spokeswoman told a news briefing in Geneva.

"Save the Children say that local reports suggest the attackers were part of the military. They describe them as AFDL," she said, using an acronym for the former rebel alliance which ousted Zairean president Mobutu Sese Seko last month.
U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan, in a speech in Harare on Monday to OAU leaders, called on Kabila to protect the refugees and secure the rule of law in the newly-named Democratic Republic of Congo.
